newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police launch hunt for Chinese illegals.
newsitem.headline: Japan police launch hunt for Chinese illegals.

text.p: Japanese police launched a manhunt on Sunday for up to 50 Chinese nationals after arresting two Chinese as fears grew of an influx of illegal immigrants.
A spokesman for Ezaki Police Station, in Yamaguchi Prefecture, southern Japan, said one of two Chinese arrested this morning told police he was part of a bigger group who had landed on Saturday.

"The suspect, Lin Yun-chin, said he came in a boat with about 50 other Chinese men and women. He said they landed together last night at a dark, uninhabited part of the coast ... We now have 120 officers scouring the area looking for possible illegal immigrants," he said.

Lin Yun-chin, 23, and companion Lin Ai-chin, 46, were arrested after police, acting on a tipoff from a local inhabitant, challenged them in Susamachi train station and gave chase when the two tried to escape, the police spokesman said.
Police are searching in the Senzaki Gulf area near Hagi on the southern Sea of Japan coast of the main Japanese island of Honshu.
The manhunt comes after Japanese Maritime Safety Agency officials last week forecast a dramatic rise in the number of illegal immigrants, particularly Chinese nationals.
Local maritime officials have called for help from neighbouring districts to try to locate the ship the alleged illegal immigrants were said to have been aboard, an agency official said.
"We have called in more than five fast patrol boats and two helicopters from neighbouring districts to help in the search for the boat. As yet there is no sign of it," he said.
Earlier on Sunday, police netted their second large haul in recent days of suspected illegal immigrants on the southern Japanese island of Kyushu, a local police spokesman said.

A spokesman for Yobuko Police Department in Saga Prefecture, Kyushu, said police arrested nine Asians cached aboard a Korean fishing boat along with another 18 foreigners still under questioning after officers searched the vessel in the town's harbour.

"We were tipped off that the boat appeared slightly suspicious and when we searched it we found 27 foreigners on board ... We arrested nine who were without passports, including the boat's South Korean skipper, Chang Hon-gu, on suspicion of attempting to enter the country illegally. We are still questioning the remaining 18," he said.
The nine suspects included five Koreans, two Bangladeshis and two Pakistanis. Another 13 Pakistanis, three Iranians and two Bangladeshis were still being questioned, he added.

"The fishing boat left the South Korean port of Yosu early yesterday morning and arrived here last night. We still don't know where the suspected illegal immigrants were headed for in Japan, or if they had a safe house or "connection" waiting for them," the official said.

The haul follows Wednesday's arrests of 58 illegal Chinese immigrants off Cape Daiozaki in Mie Prefecture, on the island of Honshu after a 230 km (125 mile) chase at sea off the Pacific coast of Japan.
